correctness.rationale: Let U and V be the images, T=U∩V and W=U+V. The four relations are equivalent to both operators killing W. Once U,V are prescribed, the maps are uniquely determined by two independent surjections E/W→U,V, counted by S_q(d,r)S_q(d,s). Count the images by choosing W, then U≤W, then T≤U; the eligible V/T are complements of U/T in W/T. The complements are graphs of maps from an (s−u)-space to an (r−u)-space, giving q^((r−u)(s−u)). The flag identity [n choose t]_q[t choose r]_q=[n choose r]_q[n−r choose s−u]_q turns this into the stated formula. Choices exist precisely for the stated intersection and quotient-dimension constraints, including rank zero. For n=2m and r=s=m, d=u≥m forces u=m and the two surjections are isomorphisms. The proof has no characteristic restriction. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; it computes image overlap by the rank of horizontal concatenation and uses polynomial F₄ arithmetic. Its six finite test cases do not establish the general count. As a boundary check, at n=2 the formula sums to 1+(q+1)(q²−1), giving 10, 33 and 76 at q=2,3,4.
